paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is telling me. Every one of these seals gets opened by the Lamb (Revelation 6:1). Nothing in this scroll starts until He breaks the seal. The horses, the earthquake, the sky rolling up like a scroll (Revelation 6:14), none of it runs loose, because He's the One holding the scroll in this scene.

Now look at the hard part. The souls under the altar ask, "How long, O Lord, holy and true…" (Revelation 6:10), and the answer is to rest a little while longer (Revelation 6:11). I think that one hurts, because waiting is hard when things are heavy. But they're each given a white robe, and they're still under the altar (Revelation 6:9, 11). The people who stayed faithful to the word of God are not forgotten, and I know a little about waiting and being found.

Then the kings, the rich, the mighty and every slave and free man hide in the caves (Revelation 6:15). They ask, "who is able to withstand it?" (Revelation 6:17). Friend, that's the question this passage leaves you holding, and it isn't meant to scare you. It's meant to wake you up to how much it matters to be ready and to know the Lamb. Six seals are open and the scroll had seven (Revelation 5:1), so this story is not done, and my ovens stay ready.
